title.narrative: Rebuilding Social and Economic Connections between Northeast Syria Returnees and Communities in Iraq (RECONNECT)

description.narrative:
Returnees from Al Amal rehabilitation centre continue to encounter obstacles to successful reintegration in their communities. These challenges include damaged housing, limited access to essential services, social mistrust, persistent conflict-related trauma, a weakened sense of belonging, and the absence of viable economic opportunities. Female-headed households, youth, and persons with disabilities are particularly affected. If left unaddressed, these barriers risk undermining social cohesion, fuelling community tensions, and exposing returnees to exploitation by actors who promote recidivism.

Over the last two years, with support from the European Union (RISE project) and additional contributions from SIDA, the United States, Italy, and the Netherlands (CRRISA project), UNDP has facilitated the reintegration of 4,738 individuals. This includes 2,461 returnees (1,556 female, 901 male and 177 persons with disability), alongside vulnerable community members. Building on the achievements and lessons learned, the proposed "Rebuilding Social and Economic Connections Between Northeast Syria Returnees and Communities (RECONNECT)" project seeks to promote sustainable, conflict-sensitive, and peaceful reintegration for both returnees and vulnerable conflict affected local resident.

RECONNECT, will provide targeted support through three main areas of intervention:

  1. Economic livelihoods and employment opportunities for returnees and vulnerable community members.
  2. Community-based mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) to address conflict related trauma and targeted legal aid and representation for the most vulnerable beneficiaries.
  3. Capacity strengthening of national and local governance for community-based reintegration and social cohesion initiatives to enhance local capacities for conflict prevention and early warning.

The project will focus on the governorates of Anbar, Kirkuk, Ninewa, Salah al-Din, Diyala, Erbil and Baghdad, areas with high concentrations of returnees. Specific districts will be selected during the inception phase through needs assessment, to avoid duplication and ensure outreach to previously unserved returnee populations.

Implementation will be carried out in close collaboration with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement (MOMD), and coordinated with key partners such as IOM, UNICEF, GCERF, CHEMONICS and organisations receiving support from ECHO in the provision of legal aid. UNDP will also work through NGO responsible parties and grantees.
